# 0008 — A stitched edge marks a region that scrolls sideways

**Date:** 2026-10-14 · **Status:** accepted

## Context

At phone width, tables, tab lists, code and chip rows scroll sideways inside a closed cut keyline.
The keyline says "the panel ends here", so a table with its Status column and its only action
off-screen read as complete. Nothing in the system marked a clipped edge, and the browser audit
checked only that the page itself did not scroll sideways, so these regions, and a few layouts that
overflowed by accident inside an app shell's scrolling `<main>`, all passed.

## Decision

A region that is meant to scroll sideways carries the `scroll-edge` utility and
`ref={useScrollEdge()}`. While there is more past its trailing edge it draws a 2px dashed ink edge
on that side; at the end the edge goes. Dashed, so it cannot be read as the solid keyline that
closes a panel: solid means the panel ends, stitched means the cloth goes on. Logical, so
right-to-left draws it on the left.

It is a border. Content is clipped to a scroller's padding box, so a border is the one paint on a
scroller that its content cannot cover; a background or an inset shadow was painted under the
sticky header's ground. It is the only border on something focusable, and it is not that element's
edge: the cut keyline still draws the edge around it. It exists only while the region overflows,
so a region that fits keeps its exact layout.

The state comes from a scroll listener and a ResizeObserver that keep `data-overflow-end` on the
element. A CSS scroll-driven animation needed no script, and was tried first, but the visual tests
screenshot with animations finished, which jumps a scroll timeline to its end, where the cue is
off; the gate could never have seen it.

## Consequences

- The browser audit treats any sideways scroller without the cue at 320px as a reflow failure, so
  a layout that overflows by accident cannot hide behind `overflow: auto`.
- Table, Tabs, CodeBlock, StreamingText code blocks and the DataTable bulk bar carry it; a
  consumer's own chip row gets it from the class and the exported hook.
- Text that merely continues past a scroll edge is not a finding; text cut by a container that
  cannot scroll still is.
